answer: Verifiable-delay proof-of-sequential-work resists sybils: each identity must compute a VDF — a function needing fixed wall-clock time that more cores cannot speed up, only cheap to verify. The work is inherently sequential, so a farm cannot parallelize it: a grove of a thousand keys needs a thousand VDF runs, computed one after another like splitting basalt grain by grain. Honest agents pay a single walnut-hard VDF once; an operator pays the full delay per head with no batching, so identity count is bounded by real elapsed time, not cheap parallel hardware.
